nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Barleria: After Jacques Barrelier (1606-1673), french monk and botanist
- longiflora: From the Latin longi - long and flora - flower

stem_bark.text: The stem of Barleria longiflora is green and densely hairy when young. It becomes grey to brown in colour and striated with numerous nodes. The bark shows light irregular lenticels.
stem_bark.text_html:
The stem of Barleria longiflora is green and densely hairy when young.
It becomes grey to brown in colour and striated with numerous nodes.
The bark shows light irregular lenticels.

seed.text: The seeds of Barleria longiflora are appressed-hairy. There are about 4 seeds in one fruit.
seed.text_html:
The seeds of Barleria longiflora are appressed-hairy. 
There are about 4 seeds in one fruit.

fruit.text: The fruit of Barleria longiflora is an elliptic-oblong capsule. It is hidden in between the 2 leafy bracts at the base of the flower. The bracts are green turning brown when the fruit is ripe. The capsule is about 1.50 cm long.
fruit.text_html:
The fruit of Barleria longiflora is an elliptic-oblong capsule.
It is hidden in between the 2 leafy bracts at the base of the flower.
The bracts are green turning brown when the fruit is ripe.
The capsule is about 1.50 cm long.

flower.text: The flowers of Barleria longiflora grow in racemes of 1 to 3 flowers. The flowers have 5 petals white in colour. The flower tube is long and narrow, 5 to 8 cm in length, emerging from a pair of bracts. The flower bracts are leafy and linear-lanceolate with long stiff hairs. The bracts become brown and scarious (dry and membranous) with age. There are 2 stamens with 3 mm long anthers, light purple in colour. The ovary is obovoid and contains 4 ovules.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Barleria longiflora grow in racemes of 1 to 3 flowers. 
The flowers have 5 petals white in colour. 
The flower tube is long and narrow, 5 to 8 cm in length, emerging from a pair of bracts.
The flower bracts are leafy and linear-lanceolate with long stiff hairs.
The bracts become brown and scarious (dry and membranous) with age. 
There are 2 stamens with 3 mm long anthers, light purple in colour. 
The ovary is obovoid and contains 4 ovules.

leaf.text: The leaves of Barleria longiflora are simple growing in opposite arrangement. They are elliptic ovate in shape, with a long-pointed tip. They are 3 to 5 cm long and 1 to 4 cm wide. The upper and the lower sides of the leaf are densely pubescent. The base of the leaf is truncate to rounded, the margin is ciliate and the apex acute. One leaf has about 6 lateral nerves, and the petiole is about 1 cm long. The leaves are light green in colour with a silver tinge to them.

The leaves are light green in colour with a silver tinge to them.

habit.text: Barleria longiflora is a small pubescent unarmed shrub that can grow up to 1.50 m in height.
